subject: Sprocket launch: quota guardrail & peak traffic playbook
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-15 09:12 PDT
Subject: Sprocket launch: quota guardrail & peak traffic playbook

Team —

Sprocket (external) just confirmed a hard launch on 2026-09-06. They expect a staged roll from 10% → 50% → 100% over 72 hours. I attached their latest forecast (sprocket_peak_forecast_v3.xlsx) and a short operations playbook (sprocket-mhap-playbook-v1.md). Key asks from Sprocket:

- Short-term quota bump (per-minute tokens and concurrent model sessions) to cover 3x expected peak for the first 48 hours.
- A temporary route-level rate-limit exemption for the top critical endpoint during canary hours.
- Clear rollback/fallback route to a smaller model if latency or error rate crosses thresholds.

Questions for you:
1) Aditya — do these numbers look realistic from the serving side? Any redlines on per-VM limits?
2) Karthik — can we do a route-level soft-exemption (not global) for 72 hours and still keep autoscaling safe?
3) Lauren — can you prepare a customer-facing mutual action plan and a single doc we can push to procurement?

Goal: Have internal sign-off + ops ticket to capacity (and a console quota add request) by EOD Friday (2026-08-20).

Thanks —
Mina
Mina Haddad
Senior Sales Ops | Redwood Inference
attachment: sprocket_peak_forecast_v3.xlsx (xlsx)
attachment: sprocket-mhap-playbook-v1.md (md)
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-16 10:04 PDT
Subject: Re: Sprocket launch: quota guardrail & peak traffic playbook

Mina — quick read through the forecast. High-level notes:

- The token/sec numbers are plausible but the concurrency per model session is tight on our current c5-train class. We should plan for a mix: reserve dedicated instances for the first 24h and allow burst autoscaling afterwards.
- Route-level soft-exemptions are doable, but we need to pin a max burst factor (I recommend max 4x baseline) and a hard cutoff at 8x to prevent noisy neighbor impact.
- KV cache eviction patterns: their payload sizes suggest a high KV working set; if they fully ramp, we may see cache churn that increases tail latency. Suggest enabling prefix caching for the critical route and a short TTL (30s) to help.

Action items:
- I'll open an ops ticket for dedicated capacity and include a recommended instance mix + expected billing delta.
- Karthik, please confirm autoscaler policy constraints.

Aditya
Aditya Rao
Runtime Lead, Serving

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-17 14:28 PDT
Subject: Re: Sprocket launch: quota guardrail & peak traffic playbook

All —

We can implement a route-level soft-exemption scoped by API key and path. Caveats:
- Soft-exemption will bypass token rate-limiter but still counts against per-VM concurrency. We should therefore request dedicated capacity for the launch window.
- Autoscaler policies: we can allow an aggressive burst policy for 72 hours, but the fastest scale-up path requires pre-warmed standby instances; otherwise, you get a 30–90s spin-up window.

I'll draft the autoscaler policy snippet and include the exact Go/JSON config we push to infra. Aditya — if you can list the exact instance types and counts, I can map to autoscaler options.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Product Engineer, Platform

From: Elaine Park <elaine@sprocket.io>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Redd <tom@sprocket.io>
Date: 2026-08-19 08:37 PDT
Subject: Re: Sprocket launch: quota guardrail & peak traffic playbook

Mina / Lauren —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. A few clarifications from our side:
- The 3x cushion is a hard requirement for our internal launch (we cannot risk a throttled experience during day-one press).
- We intend to ramp to 50% in the first 12 hours, not 72 — this shortens the window and increases the importance of pre-warms.
- If possible, we'd like a documented SLA exception (48h) that guarantees no throttling for the top endpoint; we'll sign an addendum if needed.

We attached a sample traffic curve (same file in the deck) and the release timeline. Please let us know if the 50% in 12h makes the 3x request infeasible.

Elaine Park
Head of Platform, Sprocket, Inc.

> On Aug 17, 2026, at 2:28 PM, Karthik Iyer wrote:
> > All —
> > We can implement a route-level soft-exemption scoped by API key and path...
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@sprocket.io>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-22 15:40 PDT
Subject: Re: Sprocket launch: quota guardrail & peak traffic playbook

Elaine — thanks for the details and timeline. We've updated the mutual action plan and the ops playbook to reflect the compressed ramp. Next steps: 

1) Internal approvals: Mina (sales ops) to confirm pricing addendum and Lauren to send final MAA to Sprocket by EOD 08/23.
2) Capacity ops ticket: Aditya to file for dedicated pool reservation (pre-warm nodes + 4x burst cap, hard cutoff 8x).
3) Console quota request: Mina to submit the temporary per-minute token quota increase and session concurrency bump for the critical route (72h window starting 2026-09-06 08:00 UTC).
4) Fallback plan: If tail P95 latency > 1.2s for more than 5 minutes, we will auto-failover traffic for the top 10% to a smaller L1 model and open the emergency channel.

Elaine — attached is the signed MAA draft (placeholder) and a link to the ops ticket once we open it. If that aligns, can you confirm by close of business tomorrow so we can execute procurement?

Best —
Lauren Bishop
Customer Success Lead, Redwood Inference
